title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
claim: Controlled 3d-4f cluster growth is pursued by limiting hydrolysis of hydrolysis-prone rare-earth and transition-metal ions with protecting ligands, rather than allowing unrestricted hydroxo/oxo bridging.
explanation: The review states that current 3d-4f construction mainly follows metal-ion hydrolysis and hydroxyl or oxo bridges, which is hard to control. Ligand protection is presented as the strategy that has produced many structurally diverse clusters.
conditions: Hydrolytic assembly in the presence of ligands that limit the extent of metal-ion hydrolysis.
caveats: The review does not claim that ligand protection fully eliminates uncontrolled hydrolysis.
